<!-- title: v2.0.8 – Fix monitor reports ("Argument types do not match") -->
**Bug-fix release from the lab dry run of 2.0.7: the monitor writes its JSON and HTML reports again, the Verify step of `Install-SoaToolkit.ps1` completes, and the scheduled monitor saves its status on every host.**

> The end-to-end lab validation of the 2.x scripts (L1-L20) is in progress ([docs/VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.8/docs/VALIDATION.md)). Validate in your own lab first.

## Fixed

Found in the lab with 2.0.7; the code is the same since at least 2.0.5.

- **`Watch-CloudUserConformance.ps1 -Scope All` stopped with "Argument types do not match"** after the list of provisioned users. This also ended `Install-SoaToolkit.ps1 -Step Verify` and `-Step All` with this error.
  - Cause: in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, `@(...)` around a `List[object]` created with `New-Object` throws this exception. The monitor used it for its JSON report, and the HTML table function for its rows.
  - Effect: only the CSV files were written. `Export-SoaReport.ps1` found no monitor report for L5, L6, L18 and L20.
- **The scheduled monitor on the hosts never saved `Status\monitor.json`.** The same expression failed there silently. Events were written, but `Export-SoaReport.ps1` showed no scheduled monitor result for L18.

## New

- `tools/Test-SoaScriptScope.ps1` reports `@()` around a `List[object]`. Run against 2.0.7, it finds both lines.

## Upgrade from 2.0.7

1. Replace the toolkit files and keep your `SoaToolkit.config.psd1`; there are no new keys.
2. Run `.\Install-SoaToolkit.ps1 -Step All -WhatIf`, then without `-WhatIf`. **DeployTasks** puts the fixed monitor on every host; the other steps report SAME.
3. Repeat the dry run for L2 and run `Watch-CloudUserConformance.ps1 -Scope All -Html` for L5, L6 and L20.

Details: [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/blob/v2.0.8/CHANGELOG.md)

## Verify the download

Compare the SHA-256 of the asset with the digest GitHub shows next to it. The zip contains `SHA256SUMS.txt` for every file. A build of the same tag has the same contents digest (SHA-256 of `SHA256SUMS.txt`, shown in the job summary of the release workflow).

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\cloudsync-soa-toolkit-2.0.8.zip -Algorithm SHA256
Get-ChildItem -Recurse | Unblock-File
```

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/mayer-bautechnik/cloudsync-soa-toolkit/compare/v2.0.7...v2.0.8
